name: Bloodstone Fen
description: The floor of the jungle is damp and uninviting to anyone but thirsty beasts. In one particularly deep chasm lies the remnants of a powerful magical stone, said to be a relic from the time when the gods walked on Tyria. Not even the voracious vegetation of the Maguuma will grow upon its surface.

name: The Wilds
description: The Maguuma Jungle is perhaps the most dangerous place on the continent of Tyria. The Krytans don't often venture inside its borders, and those who do are seldom heard from again. Stories of man-eating plants and gigantic insects are commonly told around the campfires and inside the huts of the local villages; most of the time to scare little children from wandering into its clinging vines.

name: Aurora Glade
description: A long time ago, a tribe of human druids ventured into the jungle to make their peace with the jungle. For many years they lived in harmony with the Maguuma, making their home in the Aurora Glade. Though there are rumors, no one has actually seen or heard from any of the druids in over a hundred years.

name: Gates of Kryta
description: Once embroiled in a devastating war with Orr and Ascalon, Kryta is now the only thriving human kingdom left on the continent of Tyria. Travelers venturing here from over the treacherous Shiverpeak Mountains will find themselves in the foothills outside the grand city of Lion's Arch.

name: D'Alessio Seaboard
description: Once called the Eastbury Reserve, this stretch of coastal land was renamed after the last Guild War. Its namesake, Saul D'Alessio, was the founder of the White Mantle and is thought by many to be the savior of Kryta.

name: Divinity Coast
description: The Divinity Coast is the site of several of this region's oldest settlements. Humans have occupied these lands for over seven hundred years. Many generations of Krytan fishermen have grown up trolling the same sacred waters of the Giant's Basin, the huge saltwater lake that defines the northern edge of the coast.

name: Talmark Wilderness
description: Talmark Wilderness

name: The Black Curtain
description: The Black Curtain

name: Sanctum Cay
description: This beautiful harbor is a favorite landing for cargo ships traveling to Kryta from the nation of Cantha. To the southeast lie the ruins of an ancient monastery said to have been the first to teach the art of Smiting Prayers, marking the transformation for Krytan Monks from passive healers to aggressive defenders of the land.

name: Droknar's Forge
description: Long ago, when the tribes of Deldrimor were united under one banner, Droknar's Forge was the seat of the mighty Dwarven nation's power.  Named for one of its most beloved kings, the Forge has never once been taken by an enemy nation.

name: The Frost Gate
description: The Frost Gate was built by the Deldrimor Dwarves as a way to protect their homes from invaders coming through Borlis Pass. When civil war broke out, the gate fell into the hands of the Stone Summit, a xenophobic group of Dwarven renegades who are trying to overthrow King Jalis Ironhammer. Now, no one gets through the pass unless the Summit allows it.

name: Ice Caves of Sorrow
description: The area surrounding this Dwarven city is dotted with numerous icy caverns that, when the wind whips through them, make a mournful sound reminiscent of a crying woman. Waterways, frozen solid year round, wind through the land here, but the resourceful Dwarves have found a way to navigate them by building large ships that skate atop the ice.

name: Thunderhead Keep
description: Within the last generation, Thunderhead Keep has become the capital of the Deldrimor nation. Since the Stone Summit uprising, it has served double duty as both the royal court to King Jalis Ironhammer and as the last line of defense for the good Dwarves of Deldrimor.

name: Iron Mines of Moladune
description: Centuries ago the city of Moladune is said to have lain here in the southern Shiverpeak Mountains. A shining place of ice and stone, legends say that it stood for thousands of years, then fell one bright dawn in a single earthshaking crash, leaving behind no sign of its inhabitants. Today, the mines are the only sign that the city might once have been more than myth.

name: Borlis Pass
description: The Shiverpeaks rise up over ten-thousand feet above sea level. In the shadow of this enormous mountain range lie the kingdoms of Kryta to the west and Ascalon to the east. Borlis Pass is the closest travelable passage through the mountains to the city of Rin. The next closest lies much farther north, deep in Charr territory.

name: The Great Northern Wall
description: The Great Northern Wall is the last line of defense between the beastlike Charr of the north, and the two remaining cities of the fallen kingdom of Ascalon. Before the Searing, the Northern Gate was the grand, diplomatic entrance used to greet visiting dignitaries. Now it is just another outpost, manned by the Ascalon army and citizens who volunteer for guard duty.

name: Fort Ranik
description: Fort Ranik was the facility used by the Ascalon military to train new soldiers to fight in the Guild Wars. When the wars ended, the fort itself, like most other buildings in Ascalon, had been almost completely destroyed. All that remains are the outer walls and the memories of what once was.

name: Ruins of Surmia
description: Just outside of the Great Northern Wall lie the ruins of a once great city. This was Surmia, one of the kingdom's cultural and economic centers. Built in a time of great optimism, the founders laughed at any who criticized the wisdom of placing a city outside the protection of the Wall.

name: Nolani Academy
description: None of Ascalon's academies of magic remain intact after the Searing. In its prime, the academy in Nolani was known all across Tyria as one of the most prestigious schools of magic on the entire continent. Ambassadors from Orr and Kryta often made special arrangements to have their children study here, even though they were not of Ascalon decent.

name: Ember Light Camp
description: Just on the edge of the Ring of Fire, the Ember Light Camp was established by a group of sailors whose corsair was shipwrecked here during a terrible storm. There is little left today of the original camp except the story of the men who lived to tell the tale.

name: Grendich Courthouse
description: The one-time seat of judicial power in Grendich village, the formerly grand courthouse is now in shambles.

name: Augury Rock
description: Surrounded by mysterious pillars like stone guardians, this overlook is named for the immense crag that looms in the distance, beckoning any brave enough to approach. Do not be deceived: the rock guards its secrets well.

name: Sardelac Sanitarium
description: Once an abbey dedicated to Dwayna, Sardelac Sanitarium is now used to house those who have suffered serious mental harm during the Searing.

name: Piken Square
description: In years past, Piken Square was a bustling market where farmers and merchants would come to hock their wares. Its ruined stalls are all that remain.

name: Henge of Denravi
description: The Henge of Denravi was once a sacred meeting place for the druids of Maguuma. It fell into disuse after the druids mysteriously disappeared more than a decade ago. The only way to enter the Henge is to be granted access through the Henge Gate, and only those who have already been to Denravi can find their way back.

name: Test Map
description: This is a debug map to allow testing of species art.

name: Senji's Corner
description: Locals have dubbed this section of town "Senji's Corner," for the eccentric old man who lives there. Most think his odd riddles nothing but the ramblings of an insane man, but those who take the time to listen can learn new paths....

name: Burning Isle
description: The true power in Tyria lies within the guilds. Here, organized teams challenge each other to settle disputes or simply prove their dominance.

name: Lion's Arch
description: The seat of power in Kryta, Lion's Arch housed the royal palace of King Doric and his line until after the last Guild War. Now, the White Mantle run the city. The old buildings have all been razed, making space for barracks and more practical structures.

name: Cursed Lands
description: Cursed Lands

name: Bergen Hot Springs
description: The healing properties of these hot springs are renowned across the continent of Tyria. Pilgrims travel from all corners in hopes of being cured of what ails them, from rheumatism to gut rot to demonic possession. Water taken from the Bergen Hot Springs is a key ingredient in potions and salves used by village medics far and wide.

name: Riverside Province
description: The Ullen River originates from the farthest south of the Footprint Lakes. The river flows west into the jungle, then turns decidedly south at the Henge of Denravi. Its swift currents and shallow inlets would make it an ideal trading river but for the fact that there are few settlements on its banks.

name: Tournament 6
description: Legends speak of a Hall of Heroes that lies at the heart of the Underworld. It is said that mortals who win their way to the Hall gain the power, wisdom, and wealth of the great heroes of ages past.

description: Legends speak of a Hall of Heroes that lies at the heart of the Underworld. It is said that mortals who win their way to the Hall gain the power, wisdom, and wealth of the great heroes of ages past.

name: Broken Tower
description: Control the Tower.

name: House zu Heltzer
description: One of the oldest and largest of the Kurzick Houses, the zu Heltzers can trace their lineage to Saint Viktor and well beyond, a fact that they waste no opportunity to mention to newcomers. As masters of thought, magic, and architecture, their buildings are nothing short of exquisite, and getting past their magical wards and protections is nothing short of miraculous.

name: The Courtyard
description: Legends speak of a Hall of Heroes that lies at the heart of the Underworld. It is said that mortals who win their way to the Hall gain the power, the wisdom, and the wealth of the great heroes of ages past.

name: Unholy Temples
description: Only divine intervention will deliver you from this place.

name: Burial Mounds
description: The way through the Underworld is a labyrinth of roads, rivers, and bridges. Around every turn lies another conflict.

name: Ascalon City
description: The largest city and cultural center of this now-ruined empire, Ascalon City is one of only two remaining in the entire kingdom. Though the buildings have fallen and the cathedrals are a shambles, the people here live on in the shadow of what once was.

name: Tomb of the Primeval Kings
description: Legends remain of noble spirits who stand watch over the tombs. If there is a passage between the mortal world and the Underworld, surely such spirits would know how to find it.

name: The Vault
description: Great hordes of treasure may be found near the base of the Hall of Heroes.

name: The Underworld
description: The way through the Underworld is a labyrinth of roads, rivers, and bridges. At every turn lies another conflict.

name: Ascalon Arena
description:
For hundreds of years, heroes of all stripes have been coming to the Arenas in times of peace to practice and hone their skills. The Ascalon Arena is one of the best places for new heroes to train and learn the basics of arena combat.

name: Sacred Temples
description: Only divine intervention will deliver you from this place.

name: The Amnoon Oasis
description: For travelers into the desert, this tiny harbor represents a last chance to rest and resupply. It also provides one last view of water, the sight of which becomes increasingly rare as one ventures eastward.

name: Dunes of Despair
description: The barren desert landscape here is broken only by tall, surprisingly urban-like ruins that mark a people's failed attempt at Ascension. Made of wood from the ships that brought them to the desert's shores and bricks made of sand and mud, the structures have withstood the harsh desert weather surprisingly well. The people who built them, unfortunately, did not....

name: Thirsty River
description: One look at this dry and desolate gorge tells the tale of its naming. Where once flowed a mighty river that shaped the land over millennia, now wind and sand make their way along deep channels, now little more than an echo of the past.

name: Elona Reach
description: This desolate outpost overlooks the skeletal remains of what might once have been a bustling seaport. Brackish puddles are all that remain of the water that once meant life to fishermen and traders alike. Today, rotted pilings and tattered sailcloth are all that mark this ghost harbor.

name: The Dragon's Lair
description: The great dragon prophet, Glint, is not easy to find, for she uses powerful magics to make her lair inside a single crystalline grain of sand. A person could search a hundred lifetimes and never find the exact grain. The only true entrance is through this portal, beyond the challenges of Augury Rock.

name: Ring of Fire
description: The large volcano at the center of this ring is where the gods reportedly dropped the legendary Bloodstones before leaving Tyria for good. Of the volcanic islands that surround this one, many are still active. Ships that pass by the Ring report hearing the tell-tale hiss of scalding hot lava hitting the ocean, instantly vaporizing the saltwater into steam.

name: Abaddon's Mouth
description: The largest volcano in the Ring of Fire Island Chain, Abaddon's Mouth is rumored to be the gateway into the Underworld. But only demons and devils would dare enter the fiery chasm. All others risk being burned to cinders before even getting to the magma's edge.

name: Hell's Precipice
description: The switchback route that runs along the ridge of Abaddon's Mouth is known to any who have ventured here as Hell's Precipice. One look into the caldera of the furious volcano will explain why.

name: Titan's Tears
description: Sunken in the caldera lay the pools of bubbling lava that mark the Titan's Tears. Many prophecies end here, not always as the prophet had fortold.

name: The Eternal Grove
description: For centuries the Kurzicks have gathered in the Eternal Grove to perform the ritual known as the Awakening. Outsiders are seldom allowed to witness this ceremony, so very little is know about it, except that this is how Kurzicks create the great Forest Defenders who defend their lands from their enemies, the Luxons.

name: Lutgardis Conservatory
description: Previously known as Cypress Hollow, the Lutgardis House decided to build its cathedral and homes here after House founder, Lord Rolf Lutgardis, came to this spot seeking guidance from the gods. According to legend, Lord Lutgardis was deep in prayer when a tree, weighed down by its heavy petrified limbs, finally gave way and crashed to the forest floor. It missed Lord Lutgardis by mere inches and was immediately declared a sign from the gods that this was a blessed place to all members of House Lutgardis.

name: Vasburg Armory
description: The Vasburgs are brilliant military strategists and fighters. Their armory, which is the largest of its kind in Echovald, it is filled with powerful weapons, murals of famous battles, and the spoils of years of warring against the Luxons.

name: Serenity Temple
description: Once the largest in Ascalon, Serenity Temple was the only holy site in Ascalon dedicated to all five Tyrian gods: Dwayna, Balthazar, Grenth, Melandru, and Lyssa. Destroyed in the Searing, the priests and priestesses of the temple try their best to carry on, though the temple is now nearly indistinguishable from the surrounding rubble.

name: Ice Tooth Cave
description: Just outside of Ice Tooth Cave, Dwarven clan leaders held parley at Anvil Rock, a sacred site said to have been the forge of the Great Dwarf himself. The Dwarven clans no longer meet for purposes of peace, and no one holds out hope that the Great Dwarf will ever return to Tyria, so this icy place receives few visitors.

name: Beacon's Perch
description: Named for the legendary Dwarven warrior who single-handedly held off the great hill giant invasion of 534 A.E., Beacon's Perch runs north and south through the Shiverpeak Mountains. Today, this treacherous pass is patrolled by the Stone Summit, and as such is considered hostile to human travelers.

name: Yak's Bend
description: So called because of the numerous yak herds that rove throughout the area, Yak's Bend is the last refuge for travelers who are about to undertake the rough passage through the Shiverpeaks. Because of its lower altitude, the weather here is somewhat less harsh, providing a place to rest, regroup, and re-equip.

name: Frontier Gate
description: One of the few working gates left in the Great Northern Wall, Frontier Gate marks the border between the remaining survivors of Ascalon and the lands to the north, now occupied by the Charr. Few venture past this point, and those who do rarely return to tell of their travels.

name: Beetletun
description: Historians speculate that in time out of mind, these now-ruined watchtowers guarded Kryta from some unknown northern threat. Now the crumbled towers stand like ancient stone soldiers still awaiting the arrival of that mysterious enemy from across the great saltwater lake called the Giant's Basin.

name: Fishermen's Haven
description: This beautiful cove is said to be the home to the best fishing in all of Kryta. Legends tell of a time when the fish were so plentiful here that one had only to skim the surface with a net to take in the equivalent of a full day's catch from any other body of water. Whether the legends be true or not, Krytan fishermen, both professional and casual, can often be found on the shores of Fishermen's Haven.

name: Temple of the Ages
description: From time immemorial the Temple of the Ages has stood in this protected location just inland of the Divinity Coast. The elements have taken their toll on the temple, and even the statues of the gods are now little more than piles of rubble. Still, this sacred place holds a magic that attracts the bold and the adventurous. Some say that the stones themselves will rise up one day and rebuild the temple, and on that day, the gods will once again turn their gaze upon Kryta.

name: Ventari's Refuge
description: Named for a wise old Centaur with a penchant for peaceful living, visitors to this outpost do their business among the roots of a gargantuan stonewood tree, the largest known specimen of its kind.

name: Druid's Overlook
description: Located in the dry upper region of the Maguuma Jungle, Druid's Overlook provides a spectacular and deceptively pleasant view of the harsh and deadly Sage Lands below. This area was once home to a sacred fountain dedicated to Dwayna, whose statue now lies in pieces in the brush.

name: Maguuma Stade
description: Far from any human civilizations, Maguuma Stade is thought to have been a meeting place for the druids who long inhabited this part of the jungle. The elements and grasping vines have all but erased the evidence that anyone was ever here.

name: Quarrel Falls
description: Deep within the Maguuma Jungle lies a tiny outpost surrounded by waterfalls. So lovely and scenic is this place that adventurers often spend more time here than is strictly necessary to re-supply. Situated as it is just outside Silverwood, Quarrel Falls is like the eye of the hurricane; a calm place to rest before the storm begins once again.

name: Ascalon City
description: The largest city in the kingdom, Ascalon City is known for its beautiful architecture, numerous libraries, and bountiful shops. Because it is where many noble families make their home, it tends to receive the largest number of visitors and has become the cultural center of Ascalon.

name: Heroes' Audience
description: The ruined statues in this isolated outpost are thought to be remnants of one of the many failed civilizations the Crystal Desert has claimed. When traders first crossed the desert and established themselves amidst these fallen gods, they told one another campfire stories of how these stone figures once lived and granted favors and magics to heroes lost in these harsh lands. Hence the name, Heroes' Audience.

name: Seeker's Passage
description: Situated on the edge of the great Salt Flats, this tiny outpost is named for the Seekers, pilgrims said to have crossed the desert in search of a new home. The bones of some massive creature litters the area, a warning to the wise.

name: Destiny's Gorge
description: Once thought to be mere legend, Destiny's Gorge is a beautiful oasis in the midst of the deadly Crystal Desert. Adventurers lucky enough to make it to this outpost are treated to blue waters and lush foliage, as well as all the goods and services available at outposts throughout Tyria.

name: Camp Rankor
description: Named after the Stone Summit Dwarf Rankor Ironwill who was known for his extreme intolerance of other races, Camp Rankor had its immoral beginnings as a slave labor camp. Although it is still used to house some of its slaves, the Summit use it largely as a staging area for launching raids against the Deldrimor Dwarves.

name: The Granite Citadel
description: Located between the Stone Summit hotbeds Tasca's Demise and Spearhead Peak, the Granite Citadel is a grand fortress held by the Deldrimor Dwarves. A safe harbor in a deadly ocean of hostility, the outpost here sells relief to weary adventurers.

name: Marhan's Grotto
description: Once, Dwarves from all over the Shiverpeaks made the trek here to barter with Marhan the Mighty, a weaponsmith who was reputed for making the best axes in all the land. After he passed into the Great Forge, this grotto was named in his honor.

name: Port Sledge
description: This bustling port supplies the Dwarves with much of their goods and supplies. The dockworkers are kept busy with a constant flow of ships coming and going, and the market is always filled both with exotic and practical wares. The cold temperatures, heavy snowfall, and frozen waters make no difference to the hearty Dwarves, but travelers are wise to bring heavy coats and plenty of warm blankets.

name: Copperhammer Mines
description: Through an unfortunate twist of heritage, Ortho Copperhammer shared ownership of these mines with a cousin, Brag, a Stone Summit warlord. When Brag learned that Ortho had trade agreements with the human settlements in the foothills, he led a raid on the mines to punish his cousin. Today this area serves as an outpost for adventurers on their way to the Frozen Forest.

name: The Barradin Estate
description: Duke Barradin's family estate covers nearly two hundred hectares of Green Hills County. The duke's vineyard is known throughout Ascalon for the exquisite grapes it produces, which are used to make Amethyst, the most coveted wine in the kingdom.

name: Ashford Abbey
description: Situated just outside of the catacombs, Ashford Abbey is the resting place for many of Ascalon's most distinguished deceased citizens. On nice days, you will find the heads of many noble houses coming to this spot, paying their respects to their ancestors. It's also not uncommon to find a priest or priestess of Dwayna here, kneeling in supplication before the statue of their goddess.

name: Foible's Fair
description: This tiny bazaar lies just north of Wizard's Folly along the road to Ashford Abbey. From the shelter of its colorful tents, traders hawk their wares, trainers offer lessons, and travelers swap tales of their adventures.

name: Fort Ranik
description: Used as a training facility for the Ascalon army, Fort Ranik houses new recruits. Here, soldiers learn what it takes to be one of Ascalon's finest and bravest, and how to use their talents to defeat the enemy. Fort Ranik is one of the best-equipped strongholds in the kingdom.

Years ago, Fort Koga was a key defensive point between Kryta and the western coast of Tyria. Guilds from across Tyria came to siege its walls, for those who controlled the fort controlled the trade routes.

name: Cavalon
description: Although Cavalon is the Luxons' home settlement, most prefer to stay on the move, returning only once every decade, when the Convocation brings together all of the three armadas. Traders from around the world come to buy the precious jade and rare seashells that the Luxon merchants sell here.

name: Kaineng Center
description: This area of Cantha's sprawling northern metropolis is also sometimes called "Old Kaineng" and is usually among the first stops for visitors to the Empire of the Dragon. Before the Jade Wind, the place now called Kaineng Center actually comprised most of Kaineng City, but the ensuing population explosion as citizens fled the affected regions led to an equal expansion of metropolitan boundaries. The central district's new, official moniker was approved by imperial decree in 1408 CC.

name: Unwaking Waters
description: Previously the site of a floating temple known as Kuan Jun, the Harvest Temple, the Unwaking Waters is an immense, frozen whirlpool. When the Jade Winds passed over Cantha and Kuan Jun sunk beneath the ocean's surface, the whirlpool was formed, and like everything else in the path of the winds, became solid jade. Legends say a powerful dragon was trapped within the temple and lives there still.

name: Deldrimor War Camp
description: A dozen years ago, two Ascalon explorers, Marshalls Whitman and Tasca, planted a flag in the ground and declared this thin patch of land to be their base camp. Those days of peaceful exploration are now gone, replaced by ballistae, Deldrimor soldiers, and war yaks perched on the precipice of Grenth's Footprint.

name: Monastery Overlook
description: Shing Jea Monastery is one of the oldest and most venerated structures on the island from which it takes its name. Originally an outpost on the borderlands of the Canthan Empire, the site was saved from destruction during the Battle of Seven Barons by a favorable north wind that enshrouded it in fog. The sixth ascendant emperor then declared the outpost blessed by the gods, and the Order of Shing Jea was formed soon thereafter to serve as caretakers. It is said that the first master of the monastery, Baqualo, is buried somewhere on the grounds in an unmarked tomb.

name: Zen Daijun
description: The valley of Zen Daijun has long been a holy place to the people of Cantha and a destination for pilgrims seeking enlightenment on Shing Jea Island. It is the home of Zunraa, an ancient protector that takes the form of a Kirin. Many weary travelers have been buoyed by the restorative properties of Zunraa's ancient shrines, which still stand to this day.

name: Minister Cho's Estate
description: The Minister's Estate is the second-oldest example of classical Canthan architecture still standing on Shing Jea Island. An ever-more-extravagant series of occupants has led to steady expansion; the current estate is three times the size of the original. It still serves the purpose for which it was constructed: it is the traditional residence for the Canthan Minister of Cultural Affairs assigned to the Shing Jea Monastery and the surrounding area, a position currently held by Minister Cho. His menagerie of exotic animals from across the globe is considered to be one of the finest collections in the world.

name: Vizunah Square
description: Once home to the famous assassin Vizu, inhabitants of this neighborhood successfully petitioned the Celestial Ministry in the year 1396 to rename it in honor of the woman who had helped bring down Shiro the Betrayer.

name: Nahpui Quarter
description: Though it appears to be just another of Kaineng City's numerous slum districts, the Nahpui Quarter is actually home to the Adepts who serve Suun, the mysterious Oracle of the Mists. Within these "slums" they study the words and teachings of the Oracle while protecting the downtrodden in secret. If you wish to become Closer to the Stars, this is the place to begin.

name: Tahnnakai Temple
description: For centuries, Tahnnakai Temple has housed the souls of Cantha's most revered heroes. The bravest and most accomplished member of each profession rests here, tended by priests of the Sai Ling Order. Ornate statues line the great hall, each a stunning likeness of the hero it represents. These magnificent effigies, sculpted by Kurzick artisans, are enchanted with protective magic that guards the temple and its inhabitants from harm.

name: Arborstone
description: For centuries the zu Heltzers have expanded and remodeled their House cathedral, adding new wings and levels on a yearly basis. Recently, the Council of Nobles determined the cathedral and the area around it should have an official name, since it had grown to the size of a large town. Count zu Heltzer predictably suggested the area be called Cathedral zu Heltzer, but the other House Nobles wouldn't hear of it, and Arborstone won the final vote.

name: Boreas Seabed

The Kurzicks have managed to hold the fort against Luxon encroachment for centuries...but this arrangement may not last forever.

name: The Eternal Grove
description: For centuries the Kurzicks have gathered in the Eternal Grove to perform the ritual known as the Awakening. Outsiders are seldom allowed to witness this ceremony, so very little is known about it, except that this is how Kurzicks create the great Forest Defenders who defend their lands from their enemies, the Luxons.

name: The Jade Quarry
description: Although the Jade Sea more than lives up to its name, the jade that makes up its petrified waves is not necessarily of the best quality. The Jade Quarry has been literally carved from the stretch of seabed that contains the finest and most valuable jade derived from the mineralized bodies of countless sea creatures. Mining in the Jade Quarry is extremely dangerous, as the Kurzicks and Luxons are almost constantly fighting over this valuable resource.

name: Gyala Hatchery
description: The largest hatchery of its kind, Gyala Hatchery supplies a wide variety of eggs and hatchlings, including many species of fish and other aquatic life unavailable since the Jade Winds passed over the oceans. The hatchery is also the world's primary provider of giant turtle hatchlings, primarily for purchase by the Luxon Turtle Clan.

name: Raisu Palace
description: Emperor Senvho commissioned the rebuilding of Raisu Palace after it mysteriously burned to the ground in the year 1204, killing his father, Emperor Singtah. It took over 80 years to finish construction on the elaborate palace, but once completed, it was considered the one great achievement of Emperor Senvho's reign.

name: Imperial Sanctum
description: Only the emperor, his family, and his most trusted guards can access the inner chambers of the palace. To date, no one has ever managed to breach the walls to the sanctum, or at least lived to tell about it.

name: Unwaking Waters
description: Previously the site of a floating temple known as Kuan Jun, the Harvest Temple, the Unwaking Waters is an immense, frozen whirlpool. When the Jade Winds passed over Cantha and Kuan Jun sunk beneath the ocean's surface, the whirlpool was formed, and like everything else in the path of the winds, became solid jade. Legends say a powerful dragon was trapped within the temple and lives there still.

name: Amatz Basin
description: Long before the Great Houses formed the Council of Nobles and the Kurzick nation, Amatz Basin was the site of a fierce battle between the zu Heltzers and the Vasburgs. What they fought over, none can remember, but the fighting took a terrible toll. Even worse (from the Kurzick perspective), thousands of the dead were left to rot where they fell. In recent years, the bones of those fallen warriors have begun to resurface, and the Kurzicks blame Urgoz, a corrupted forest spirit, for these ghastly exhumations.

name: Raisu Palace
description: Emperor Senvho commissioned the rebuilding of Raisu Palace after it mysteriously burned to the ground in the year 1204, killing his father, Emperor Singtah. It took over 80 years to finish construction on the elaborate palace, but once completed, it was considered the one great achievement of Emperor Senvho's reign.

name: The Aurios Mines
description: Relics of a mysterious race, possibly an offshoot of the Deldrimor dwarves, have been uncovered in this productive jade mine. Though not as large or strategically vital as the enormous Jade Quarry, The Aurios Mines are of great importance to historians and scholars.

name: Shing Jea Monastery
description: As the ancient Canthan name implies, Shing Jea is the jewel of Cantha. Headed by the legendary Ritualist, Master Togo, the monastery provides training to students of all heroic professions, including the Ritualist and Assassin professions native to Cantha. Graduates of the Shing Jea Monastery are recognized worldwide as masters of their chosen arts.

name: Shing Jea Arena
description: By longstanding tradition, full-scale arena combat is prohibited on the rural island of Shing Jea, out of reverence for the monastery of the same name. Yet those who study at the monastery require a place to train in such arts. The solution? Shing Jea Arena, located on the tiny island of Tinnairukan south of the larger landmass...close enough to train, but separated from Shing Jea Island itself.

name: Arborstone
description: For centuries the zu Heltzers have expanded and remodeled their House cathedral, adding new wings and levels on a yearly basis. Recently, the Council of Nobles determined the cathedral and the area around it should have an official name, since it had grown to the size of a large town. Count zu Heltzer predictably suggested the area be called Cathedral zu Heltzer, but the other House Nobles wouldn't hear of it, and Arborstone won the final vote

name: Boreas Seabed
description: The site of many of the greatest battles in Luxon history, the Boreas Seabed is also the home range of Zhu Hanuku, or "Old Long-Arms" in the ancient tongue. Every year, this mammoth kraken arises from the petrified seas to lash out at the Luxon capital of Cavalon. The souls of the great Luxon champions are also said to remain here, watching over their descendants.

name: Great Temple of Balthazar
description: A sacred place for those who study the art of war. Here on the Battle Isles the Zaishen practice various types of combat from around the world.

name: Tsumei Village
description: This pastoral agricultural community has remained virtually unchanged for almost a thousand years, and its temples and farmhouses are among the oldest examples of ancient Canthan architecture in the empire. Thanks to the preservation efforts of Master Togo, wealthy tourists from Kaineng City have so far been prevented from spoiling Tsumei Village's idyllic splendor and historic buildings.

name: Seitung Harbor
description: The largest and arguably most important port in Cantha, Seitung Harbor is the point of entry for most outsiders. Ships traveling to distant Tyria and the far-flung Battle Isles depart from Seitung Harbor with dizzying regularity, while the traffic from those distant lands arrives with equal frequency. Canthans with little spare time often say they are "busy as a Seitung harbormaster." At least, in polite company.

name: Ran Musu Gardens
description: Once the private retreat of a Canthan prince whose name has been lost to history, Ran Musu ("blue moon") Gardens is now protected from settlement or development by imperial decree. The Monks of Shing Jea often visit the gardens to meditate for days at a time.

name: Sunjiang District
description: Once a business district, this area was converted into living quarters after the Jade Wind obliterated much of the countryside. As flocks of refugees made their way into Kaineng City, the Celestial Ministry sent them to Sunjiang District, where they were assigned to a street block and allowed to build a 10-foot-by-10-foot living space.

name: Nahpui Quarter
description: Though it appears to be just another of Kaineng City's numerous slum districts, the Nahpui Quarter is actually home to the Adepts who serve Suun, the mysterious Oracle of the Mists. Within these "slums" they study the words and teachings of the Oracle while protecting the downtrodden in secret. If you wish to become Closer to the Stars, this is the place to begin.

name: Urgoz's Warren
description: One of the oldest parts of the ancient Echovald Forest, this area is home to Urgoz, a spirit that once protected the forest. For unknown reasons, Urgoz has since turned on the forest and its inhabitants, though the Kurzicks speculate it might have something to do with the Jade Wind.

name: Altrumm Ruins
description: The vast ruins of Altrumm are thought by most historians to be all that remains of the first great Kurzick city, destroyed by some ancient and mysterious catastrophe. The Kurzicks themselves claim their ancestors did not build the structures found here. If this is true, then Altrumm certainly influenced Kurzick architectural sensibilities.

name: Zos Shivros Channel
description: Infamous for sending many sailors to their watery deaths back when ships still sailed the Jade Sea, this once-treacherous channel is now traversed mostly by Luxons as they make their way to their home settlement, Cavalon.

name: Dragon's Throat
description: The rumble of falling waste water does little to mask the unsavory business that thrives deep below Dragon's Throat. A massive sewer pipe at the far end of a subterranean hollow funnels sewage away from the prim and proper, adding insult to an already injured populace underground.

name: Isle of Weeping Stone
description: The true power in Tyria lies within the guilds. Here, organized teams challenge each other to settle disputes or simply prove their dominance.

name: Isle of Jade
description: The true power in Tyria lies within the guilds. Here, organized teams challenge each other to settle disputes or simply prove their dominance.

name: Harvest Temple
description: The site of Cantha's most infamous murder, the Harvest Temple in which Emperor Angsiyan was struck down by the treacherous Shiro Tagachi still stands. It is the geographic epicenter of the Jade Wind; a place of fear, danger, and bitter memories. Here the mighty dragon Kuunavang still lurks in the caverns beneath the temple, utterly corrupted by the proximity of Shiro's death wail.

name: Breaker Hollow
description: Formed out of the hull of a ship that was grounded during the Jade Winds, this small outpost serves as a place for Luxons to convene and trade goods.

name: Leviathan Pits
description: This relatively small but well-protected jade mine is deep within Luxon territory and is dominated by a structure built from a mammoth tortoise shell. Some of the most valuable and exquisitely preserved examples of jade fossils have been discovered here, and many can be found within Master Togo's personal collection at the Shing Jea library.

name: Isle of the Nameless
description: Hone your skills and spells. Prepare yourself for combat.

name: Zaishen Challenge
description: Test your mettle against the best fighters of the Zaishen Order.

name: Zaishen Elite
description: Entering this battle is a challenge to the Zaishen honor, they will spare no effort to see you destroyed. Are you powerful enough to take on the entire Zaishen Order?

name: Maatu Keep
description: One of the oldest sections of Kaineng City, Maatu Keep sits at the base of the Qinkaishi Mountains and serves as the city's entry point for both Luxons and Kurzicks. The keep, once a beautiful example of ancient Canthan architecture, has since fallen into neglect and disrepair.

name: Zin Ku Corridor
description: This dark, humid, and smelly corridor may not look like much, but it leads followers deep into the sewers, to Tahnnakai Temple. Some of the city's more unsavory guilds have been known to assign thugs to this corridor, who lie in wait to ambush unsuspecting passerby on their way to the temple.

name: Brauer Academy
description: Members of House Brauer meet here to gossip, debate, and host celebrations. This Kurzick House is known for its exceptionally gifted sculptors and painters, whose artwork is coveted throughout the world. A favorite Brauer pastime: meeting in the courtyard after evening prayers to display their newest pieces de'arte.

name: Durheim Archives
description: The home of the scholarly House Durheim is not far from the border with the Jade Sea, but is well-protected by the dense petrified growth of the Echovald Forest and the waters of the Rijeka River. It is said that Durheim poetry owes its beauty not just to the innate talent of its authors, but to the natural splendor of nearby Mourning Veil Falls.

name: Bai Paasu Reach
description: This small mountain town has stood in one form or another for almost eight hundred years, as can be seen by the traditional stone architecture of indisputably Canthan origin. Once a way station for weary travelers and swift-footed messengers, it has of late become a popular vacation spot for wealthy Canthan tourists who value its remote location.

name: Seafarer's Rest
description: Once a quiet destination for the Luxon elite, Seafarer's Rest now serves as a mere resting stop for weary travelers meandering across the Jade Sea. The wealthy sat perched atop towering rock structures, with every need attended to by a staff of attentive servants. Those who currently inhabit this outpost subsist on funds from odd jobs and mercenary work; though some say Seafarer's Rest will one day return to its former stature.

name: Vizunah Square (Local Quarter)
description: Once home to the famous assassin Vizu, inhabitants of this neighborhood successfully petitioned the Celestial Ministry in the year 1396 to rename it in honor of the woman who had helped bring down Shiro the Betrayer.

description: A favorite destination for locals and foreign visitors alike, this bustling marketplace is the place to find locally made trinkets, fresh produce and fish, and traditional Canthan delicacies such as pickled vermin tongue.

name: Vizunah Square (Local Quarter)
description: One of the oldest sectors of Cantha City, Courthouse Square is home to many of the capital's official buildings, including the Cantha City Courthouse, the Celestial Ministry, and the Bank of Cantha.

description: For hundreds of years, heroes of all stripes have been coming to the Arenas in times of peace to practice and hone their skills. The Ascalon Arena is one of the best places for new heroes to train and learn the basics of arena combat.

name: The Underworld
description: The way through the Underworld is a labyrinth of roads, rivers, and bridges. At every turn lies another conflict.

name: Tanglewood Copse
description: A safe haven for travelers, Tanglewood Copse lies nestled between the outer edges of southern Kaineng City and the harsh, towering Qinkaishi Mountains. According to legend, the first emperor stopped to camp here for the night during his inaugural tour of the Echovald Forest. It is now a site of pilgrimage for devotees of traditional Canthan ancestor worship.

name: Saint Anjeka's Shrine
description: Considered sacred ground to the Kurzicks, this shrine marks the spot where Saint Anjeka was struck down by raiding Luxons. Witnesses to the event that day claimed that Anjeka tried to dissuade the invaders from bloodshed by speaking of the glory of the gods, but when a Luxon spear pierced her heart in the middle of her sermon, all hope of peace was shattered.

name: Eredon Terrace
description: This remote Luxon outpost is the site of the Eredon jade-smasher apparatus, an experimental device of Canthan design that allows huge chunks of jade to be reduced to smaller size for ease of transport. A small village has sprung up around this structure.

name: Jahai Bluffs
description: These unscalable bluffs are the border between Vabbi and Kourna. The Elon river falls from its heights in the first cataract. The only pass through these bluffs is guarded by the Fortress of Jahai.

name: Kamadan, Jewel of Istan
description: Kamadan, Jewel of Istan

name: Marga Coast
description: The Marga Coast is a low coastal area north and west of Gandara. Its name derives from its original inhabitants, the Margonites.

name: Fahranur, The First City
description: The shattered remains of the first city founded by the Elonians. It was decimated and abandoned by its populace during the Scarab Plague. Only recently has excavation of this area resumed.

name: Sunward Marches
description: A dry, upland region of Kourna, the Sunward Marches are, like other regions, dominated by the local Kournan Garrison.

name: Vortex
description: The swirling vortex, unleashed by the death of Varesh Ossa, leads to the Realm of Torment.

name: Barbarous Shore
description: Barbarous Shore

name: Camp Hojanu
description: A wilderness camp of smugglers who trade with the corsairs, the camp may be rustic but is also heavily armed. Travelers are encouraged not to sneak up on the smugglers, lest their surprise visit be greeted with a surprised slaying by a nervous smuggler.

name: Bahdok Caverns
description: A maze of underground passages within Bahdok leading to Vabbi

name: Wehhan Terraces
description: These terraces were originally created by a monastic order dedicated to the goddess Dwayna. The restorative nature of the natural springs here made the location a regular stop for pilgrims. Though the order has since died out, its buildings and beautiful landscaping remains as a testament to their devotion.

name: Dejarin Estate
description: Large agricultural farm, formerly under the control of the Dejarin clan, now controlled by the Kournan government

name: Arkjok Ward
description: Heavily irrigated area of Kourna, its pumping stations provide water to more arid regions of the province.

name: Yohlon Haven
description: The hub of social and business gatherings, Yohlon Haven is located at a major viaduct and, along with water, disseminates gossip, news, and informal trade among the farmers in the area. Such gatherings have made the station moderately wealthy, and travelers will be comfortable here.

name: Gandara, the Moon Fortress
description: The great fortification at the mouth of the Elon, this is the home of its Warmarshal, Varesh Ossa. All official trade passes through its great, crescent-shaped harbor.

name: Vortex
description: This vortex leads back to the mortal realm.

name: The Floodplain of Mahnkelon
description: Located just downstream of the falls of Jahelon, this area is dominated by its waterworks.

name: Turai's Procession
description: Furthermost northern claims of the Kournans, this is a wild, dry land beyond even the reach of the Elonian viaducts. The Centaurs have been pushed back into this area, along with a few hearty settlers. It lays at the doorway to the Desolation. This was the route Turai took when he made his Grand Pilgrimage.

name: Sunspear Sanctuary
description: Carved as a shrine to Melandru in ancient times, this red-rocked vault was once used as cistern by the Kournans to contain the Elon's floodwaters. When that enterprise failed, the sanctuary was walled off and forgotten, inhabited only by things that like to live in the dark. Now it serves as a secret refuge for the Sunspears.

name: Yatendi Canyons
description: Narrow canyons form the primary trade route between Kourna and Vabbi, a labyrinthine passage that was once for only the most stalwart of traders. Time and commerce have eroded the dangerous reputation of the canyons, and now the only bandits patrolling them are the ones marking up merchandise in the caravans.

name: Chantry of Secrets
description: The Order of Whispers tends the home of the statues of the Five True Gods, while also using the Chantry as their base of operations. A secretive order, they welcome visitors but do not share much in the way of information.

name: Garden of Seborhin
description: One of the most beautiful spots in Vabbi, this area is a lovingly constructed complex of tile, fountains, and greenery that shows off the power and wealth of the Princes of Vabbi.

name: Holdings of Chokhin
description: Province ruled by Mehtu the Wise, who commands the area form the great library, the Halls of Chokhin

name: Mihanu Township
description: Prince Mehtu rules this farming community that serves as the gateway to the Holdings of Chokhin. Mehtu has arranged for every child in the village to be taught to read and write, so that some day they may join his corps of collectors and researchers who roam the world adding volumes to his ever-expanding library.

name: Vehjin Mines
description: Extensive mining operations under the control of the Vabbian princes. It was through this area that Palawa Joko invaded Vabbi, and where most of his army was destroyed after Palawa Joko's defeat.

name: Basalt Grotto
description: It has been long-rumored that there exists a safe passage between the Desolation and Vabbi, a passage discovered and used to brutal effect by Palawa Joko when he invaded. The winding passages of the grotto are known to but few, who guard that knowledge jealously, out of fear or greed.

name: Forum Highlands
description: Wild region dominated by the Grand Forum of Vab, the site of what passes for Vabbi's government. Originally the lowlands beneath the walls of the tower were inhabited by small towns and farms, but these were destroyed by Palawa Joko and not replaced.

name: Sebelkeh Basilica
description: One of the wonders of Elona, the Sebelkeh Basilica is a great floating temple of the goddess Lyssa. Visible for miles, it is a symbol of the power of the goddess in the land.

name: Resplendent Makuun
description: One of the most opulent Locations in Vabbi, this hedonistic center of indulgence is controlled by Prince Bokka the Magnificent.

name: Honur Hill
description: A rag-tag community of artists, actors, and other unsavory types, the natives of Honur Hill make their living fleecing wealthy patrons on their way to the Bokka Amphitheatre. If you need a reproduction statue of Grenth or some fake memoirs of a Prince of Vabbi, the merchants of Honur Hill will be happy to oblige you. Otherwise, hold on to your purse with both hands and walk fast.

name: Wilderness of Bahdza
description: One of the furthest points of Vabbian control, hard on the lands of the inhuman tribes, this region is dominated by a great citadel using magical bombards.

name: Sun Docks
description: Sun Docks

name: Vehtendi Valley
description: The narrow canyonlands of the south open up into the wider series of vales, where many of the regions operate large farms.

name: Yahnur Market
description: A riverside village, Yahnur has done well for itself as a stopover place for merchant crafters and visitors heading upriver to Resplendent Makuun and the Bokka Amphitheatre. Travelers are advised to bring, and to hold onto, their coin purses.

name: The Hidden City of Ahdashim
description: A great underground city built for the ancient princes of Vabbi as a safe hiding place for times of trouble.  Through the ages, it has been used to protect the prince's gold more than the princes themselves.

name: The Kodash Bazaar
description: Considered the best market in Vabbi, where the rare, the strange, and the unique are all for sale. If you can't get it here, it simply isn't worth getting. Here all of Vabbi trades, mingles, and gossips.

name: The Mirror of Lyss
description: A huge artificial lake carved out of the dry wastes of Vabbi, it is located beneath the Basilica and reflects the temple above.

name: Venta Cemetery
description: Originally a graveyard reserved for Kournans slain by Centaurs, Venta Cemetery has blossomed into a small, walled town where market stalls share space with the headstones. While the occasional Centaur will trade with "two-legs" here, the gates are locked at night and guards are posted at the walls.

name: Kamadan, Jewel of Istan
description: Kamadan is the home port for the mighty Istani navy, and the main point of landfall for ships from nearby Kourna, as well as those traveling from Cantha, Tyria, and the Battle Isles. Its deep harbor is sheltered from seasonal storms by a ridge of hills to the south. Built around relics and statues from the days of the Primeval Kings, Kamadan has earned the title, Jewel of Istan.

name: Kodonur Crossroads
description: At the crossroads of Kodonur, no one will speak ill of Warmarshal Varesh; her tight control over trade has made the merchants here rich. Come for the bargains, stay for the excellent security measures. Just don't get too rowdy, or you may find yourself on the receiving end of Varesh's famed law and order.

name: Rilohn Refuge
description: Located high above the banks of the Elon River, the Refuge is used by the nearby villagers and workers as a temporary camp. When the Elon River overflows its banks every spring to give life back to the fertile plains, the residents of the surrounding area retreat here until the floods have subsided and the land is restored once more.

name: Pogahn Passage
description: This area is dominated by one of the many heavily-manned garrisons that dot the Kournan countryside. However, the landscape around the fort is marked with caverns, chasms, and natural bridges, which the local merchants use to escape the ever-vigilant eye of Warmarshal Varesh's minions.

name: Moddok Crevice
description: A smuggler's camp hidden behind the Waterworks of Mahnkelon, the Crevice is for those who don't want to be found, those who aren't looking, and those who just want to be left alone. Residents keep to themselves and strongly suggest that you do the same.

name: Tihark Orchard
description: A small community on the edge of the Highlands, Tihark Orchard was settled by a group of retired gardeners of Seborhin. Through horticulture and careful irrigation, they have made this rugged upland bloom.

name: Consulate
description: Consulate

name: Plains of Jarin
description: These rolling hills are dominated by the Sunspear Great Hall.

name: Sunspear Great Hall
description: One of the oldest standing structures on the Istani Isles, the Sunspear Great Hall dates back to the time of Sogolon the Protector, who turned the Sunspears into an independent order devoted to the protection of all Elona. The twin, magical fountains are a tribute to the Sunspears' primeval roots, while the Great Hall stands as a memorial to the many generations of heroes forged within its walls.

name: Cliffs of Dohjok
description: Also called "Earth's End," these southern-facing bluffs are quarried for stone and semi-precious gems.

name: Dzagonur Bastion
description: The gateway to the mighty Citadel of Dzagon, the Bastion is a hub of activity for mercenaries, recruiters, and merchants of arms and armor. Locals are more than willing to sell you any manner of implements for wounding, killing, and maiming, as well as the armor to deflect other adventurer's purchases.

name: Dasha Vestibule
description: The Vestibule is the main entrance to the Hidden City of Ahdashim and serves its role well. Soaring and opulently appointed, only the princes of Vabbi usually gaze upon its splendor.

name: Grand Court of Sebelkeh
description: Gateway to the wondrous Basilica, the Grand Court overlooks the reflecting pool that gives the Mirror of Lyss its name. From here, one may ascend to the floating Sebelkeh Basilica itself, the most ornate and magical temple in Elona, and the heart of the Lyssan faith.

name: Command Post
description: Command Post

name: Joko's Domain
description: Former heart of Palawa Joko's sprawling empire.

name: Bone Palace
description: The Bone Palace... The very name strikes terror in the hearts of all Elonians. From this dark, foreboding edifice, Palawa Joko struck out across the Desolation to conquer Elona. It is said the souls of the dead enslaved by Palawa Joko still writhe within the walls, screaming for release.

name: The Ruptured Heart
description: A twisted, upheaved landscape shattered by a war of the gods, further disturbed from the loser of that war seeking to escape.

name: The Mouth of Torment
description: It was here that Abaddon and his Margonites challenged the power of the Five True Gods, and here that the other gods smote the God of Secrets down, imprisoning him and his following in a Realm of Torment. This once beautiful land is now a crater littered with the trapping of a god. And above it the Mouth of Torment hangs, a weakness in the world, a globe of pure evil, beckoning all to their doom.

name: The Shattered Ravines
description: A blasted realm left to the elements, forgotten by god and man.

name: Lair of the Forgotten
description: Time has not been kind to this last bastion of a once-great empire. The erosion caused by the outward creep of the Realm of Torment has eaten away at the very foundations of this forgotten citadel, dropping much of it into a vast sinkhole. It is said the lone living witness to the Margonite assault on the Gates of Heaven and Abaddon's defeat at the hands of the Five True Gods still resides here, all but abandoned to the mists of time.

name: Poisoned Outcrops
description: Parts of Abaddon's Realm of Torment have leaked into these lands, corrupting them further and filling its canyons with a malignant greenish glow.

name: The Sulfurous Wastes
description: A poisoned realm that has been growing over the centuries, as pockets of sulfurous gas, deadly to the living, carpet the lowlands. Only the demons, the undead, and the wurms do not seem to mind.

name: The Ebony Citadel of Mallyx
description: The Ebony Citadel of Mallyx

name: The Alkali Pan
description: A dry, desiccated landscape, hellish and empty, made worse by the recent upheavals from the Realm of Torment.

name: Cliffs of Dohjok
description: Also called "Earth's End," these southern-facing bluffs are quarried for stone and semi-precious gems.

name: Crystal Overlook
description: The closest Elonian Lands to Tyria, centuries ago it was used as a passage to the Crystal Sea, and then the Crystal Desert, to the tombs of the Primeval Kings. Now those ways are lost, and the land is riven by the power of a lost, angry god.

name: Kamadan, Jewel of Istan
description: Kamadan is the home port for the mighty Istani navy, and the main point of landfall for ships from nearby Kourna, as well as those traveling from Cantha, Tyria, and the Battle Isles. Its deep harbor is sheltered from seasonal storms by a ridge of hills to the south. Built around relics and statues from the days of the Primeval Kings, Kamadan has earned the title, Jewel of Istan.

name: Gate of Torment
description: The Gate of Torment stand upon coagulated reality extruded by the Realm of Torment into the real world. It is nothing more than a thin crust of the real world floating on the edge of the insanity that is Abaddon's prison. Beyond this gate, the forces of Abaddon must not be allowed. If the gate is sundered by the dark god, his evil will pour forth onto the world unabated.

name: Gate of Anguish
description: A tiny shred of shattered reality clinging to Abaddon's former realm, the Gate of Anguish leads to a domain of unimaginable sorrow and despair. It is here that the evil lord Mallyx the Unyielding builds his bastion of power, which threatens the very existence of the Goddess of Truth.

name: Secure the Refuge
description:
Beyond you will find the Sanctuaray. It is an ancient place, even more ancient than me, and that means it has escaped Varesh's notice for now. It should make the perfect secret base to hide from the Kournan forces while you fight the good fight. There is a catch, however...it is somewhat infested with monsters. Somewhat. Okay, a lot. But I have a plan to get rid of them.

You should take Melonni with you, she can perform an ancient cleansing ceremony that will clear the place out. It will be perfect for a base...natural caverns that can house many freedom fighters and an abandoned aqueduct that will provide fresh water.

name: Evacuation
description:
We need to get the survivors to the waiting ships in Lowlands_Country_OP, but it won't be easy without making our presence known. We've learned that the Kournan Army has just sent reinforcements from their base in Lowlands_Fort to search for us. We must hurry the Sunspears to the docks before the forces arrive. Based on scout intelligence, we know of three major obstacles. There is a garrison of Kournan troops guarding the entrance to the harbor. Most of our troops are unarmed and nearly all of them injured. We simply won't stand a chance if we're discovered. Once we pass the garrison, we'll have to contend with scout patrols making their rounds by the garrison's perimeter. If any of them spot us, we'll need to take them out quickly before they sound the alarm. Lastly, we'll have to avoid detection by the several guard posts scattered throughout the countryside. We'll need to kill the guards or simply avoid them altogether. Provided we make it past the garrison, the scouts, and the guard posts, there's no guarantee that the pirates haven't double-crossed us and sold us out to Princess Varesh's troops.

The cards are stacked against us, but in truth, we've been fighting against unfavorable odds since our arrival at Kourna. Maybe for once luck will be on our side. Are you ready?

Surrounded by corsairs and all manner of beasts and roaming plants, these hardy folk still find a way to scrape out a living farming ironreed in the local ponds and fishing the open sea. The Issnur Isles east of the village were once part of the Mehtani Keys, but years of silt brought in during storms formed land bridges, allowing the local wildlife to flourish and roam the region.

name: Heart of Abaddon
description: The prison of Abaddon, a realm made entirely of parts of reality that the God of Secrets has dragged into the depths over time. All have been corrupted, and at the heart of all is the imprisoned form of the god himself.

description: The Underworld

description: Marga Coast, once it has been replaced by its corrupted duplicate. It didn't take.

name: Nightfallen Jahai
description: Nightfallen Jahai

name: Depths of Madness
description: The Depths, poisoned by the dreams of their dark god, serve as a horrific barrier to the Heart of Abaddon. Imprisoned Margonites roam the landscape, forever toiling to make Abaddon's darkest nightmares reality.

name: Rollerbeetle Racing
description: Sent by boat from Elona, rollerbeetles are brought to this arena and its famous racetrack, and put through a rigorous training process. Only the best of the best are given the privilege to race.

name: Domain of Fear
description: Repository of fears of primitive men at the time Abaddon was imprisoned. May indicate the power of a previous, spider or dryder-like race in the world.

name: Gate of Fear
description: The Gate of Fear is one of the great locks erected by the Five Gods to imprison Abaddon, weakened by the passage of the ages and the machinations of the God of Secrets. Past this gate lies a great plane inhabited by the primal fears of early man, and swept by the winds of panic.

name: Domain of Pain
description: Place where souls damned to the Realm of Torments are converted into base spirits and stored for eternity.

name: Domain of Secrets
description: Where all the knowledge about Abaddon has been condemned to. Includes not only material existing at time of Abaddon's fall, but material generated since then by cultists and researchers.

name: Gate of Secrets
description: Beyond these gates lay the forbidden knowledge of a dark god. Here has been confined the eternal knowledge of Abaddon, hidden here to protect the real world. To know the true secrets of Abaddon is to know your own eternal torment.

name: Gate of Anguish
description: A tiny shred of shattered reality clinging to Abaddon's former realm, the Gate of Anguish leads to a domain of unimaginable sorrow and despair. It is here that the evil lord Mallyx the Unyielding builds his bastion of power, which threatens the very existence of the Goddess of Truth.

name: Jennur's Horde
description: A rugged mining camp used by workers in the Vehjin Mines, Jennur's Horde is none the less a booming outpost on payday, where miners flush with their spoils go broke again just as quickly in games of chance and impromptu taverns set up in the shadows of abandoned mining equipment.

name: Nundu Bay
description: A bustling port on the Marga Gulf used mostly by fishing vessels, Nundu Bay is an idyllic port town in almost every way. Visitors are advised to steer clear of the corsairs, literally.

name: Gate of Desolation
description: Once a mighty edifice designed to repel desert raiders like Palawa Joko, the Gates of Desolation are a broken skeleton slowly being reclaimed by the desert. A few determined traders hang on, although their customers are mostly Centaurs from the plains.

name: Champion's Dawn
description: Situated near the mineral-rich Cliffs of Dohjok, Champion's Dawn is the base of operations for the Istani Society of Engineers and Architects. The stone and gems quarried here have fueled Istani architecture for a millennium. The Primeval style has so deeply impacted modern Istani builders that the Society has a long-standing rivalry with the Excavation Corps over the status of the ruins to the west.

name: Ruins of Morah
description: The grandeur of this ancient Elonian city can still be seen amid its crumbling visage; echoes of a noble and grand purpose. Originally established to watch over the Mouth of Torment, Morah was ever a haunted place. It was abandoned two hundred years after its founding, succumbing to the spread of the desert. Recent ruptures from the crater have further destroyed this once majestic city as the Realm of Torment seeps in through the cracks in reality.

name: Fahranur, The First City
description: The shattered remains of the first city founded by the Elonians. It was decimated and abandoned by its populace during the Scarab Plague. Only recently has excavation of this area resumed.

name: Bjora Marches
description: Bjora Marches

name: Zehlon Reach
description: A settled region of Istan dominated by a shallow arm of the sea reaching southward. Most of its settlement is along the northern coast.

name: Lahtenda Bog
description: A dark, swampy region kept in eternal shade by overhanging tree moss, this area is a favorite haunt for tomb-robbers and corsairs hoping to avoid the official eye of Istan's protectors.

name: Arbor Bay
description: Arbor Bay

name: Issnur Isles
description: Originally a string of islands similar to the Mehtani Keys, the shallows have been bridged and turned into low ponds.

name: Beknur Harbor

Surrounded by corsairs and all manner of beasts and roaming plants, these hardy folk still find a way to scrape out a living farming ironreed in the local ponds and fishing the open sea. The Issnur Isles east of the village were once part of the Mehtani Keys, but years of silt brought in during storms formed land bridges, allowing the local wildlife to flourish and roam the region.

name: Mehtani Keys
description: A string of low islands linked by shallow waterways, Mehtani Keys is noted for its nearby reefs, frequent storms, and numerous sharks.

name: Kodlonu Hamlet
description: The annual storms that wash over the Mehtani Keys force residents of Kodlonu Hamlet to rebuild on a regular basis. Thus, this central marketplace for the keys and the Issnur Isles is dominated by tent-and-pole construction. Most merchants merely fish their old, stained tents from the surf and begin anew each season, selling wares only found in the keys, specialty items from afar that have somehow bypassed Kamadan's customs, and lost cargo "rescued" from the corsairs.

name: Island of Shehkah
description: The Tutorial

name: Jokanur Diggings
description: This camp, just outside the ruins of the fabled First City of Fahranur, is headquarters to the Istani Provincial Excavation Corps. Fahranur, decimated and abandoned during the Scarab Plague, was the ancient home of the Primeval Kings who once ruled all Elona. Some believe it also holds the key to the mystery of the Scarab Plague's origin. Superstitious fears and a bitter rivalry between the Excavation Corps and the Society of Engineers have kept work on this important archaeological site stagnant until recently.

name: Blacktide Den
description: This campsite at the edge of the Lahtenda Bog is a haven for all manner of shady characters and black market business. From corsairs attempting to escape justice to tomb-robbers looking to pawn their ill-gotten booty, to the odd Necromancer simply interested in the death and decay of the swampy bayou to the south, Blacktide Den provides the perfect meeting place: dark, dangerous, and remote.

name: Consulate Docks
description: These docks, located behind the imposing Consulate building at the northern end of Kamadan, are used solely for official government business. They can only be accessed through the Consulate, and then only with written approval. Elders traveling to the Elonian mainland, as well as ambassadors from Kourna and Vabbi, depart from here, bypassing the chaos of the common docks, which are used for trade vessels and tourists.

name: Gate of Pain
description: Any hero arriving at the Gate of Pain knows that they lead nowhere except to pain and destruction...destruction of sanity, hope, joy, and ultimately, an end to life itself. Beyond these gates the souls of those touched by Abaddon are imprisoned, their existence drained they are nothing more than spirits who have forgotten their offense and their previous life.

name: Gate of Madness
description: Those who stand at the Gate of Madness stand at the end of their own grasp on reality, because within, the vision of the dark god rules, and the twisted visions that his eyes have beheld will become the visions of all who pass through the gate. Nothing else remains except infinite, screaming madness.

name: Abaddon's Gate
description: The unimaginable torture and loneliness to which the Five Gods abandoned their dark sibling lies within Abaddon's Gate. He strains against his chains and his anguish resounds throughout the Realm of Torment, twisting and mutilating the minds and souls of all who venture near.

name: Sunspear Arena
description: Built shortly after the Sunspears withdrew from Dynastic service, this arena serves as a place for Sunspear heroes and new inductees to hone their fighting abilities.

name: The Astralarium
description: The Astralarium, sitting high atop the bluffs of northern Istan, is home to the astronomically oriented Order of the Sky. This open-air laboratory, with its multiple solar reflectors and pedestal-mounted astrolabes, is the center of astrological and astronomical study in Elona. Scholars from all three provinces flock to the Zehlon Reach to study under the stars at the Astralarium and try to divine the meaning of ancient, dark prophecies.

name: Shing Jea Monastery
description: As the ancient Canthan name implies, Shing Jea is the jewel of Cantha. Headed by the legendary Ritualist, Master Togo, the monastery provides training to students of all heroic professions, including the Ritualist and Assassin professions native to Cantha. Graduates of the Shing Jea Monastery are recognized worldwide as masters of their chosen arts.

name: Seitung Harbor
description: The largest and arguably most important port in Cantha, Seitung Harbor is the point of entry for most outsiders. Ships traveling to distant Tyria and the far-flung Battle Isles depart from Seitung Harbor with dizzying regularity, while the traffic from those distant lands arrives with equal frequency. Canthans with little spare time often say they are "busy as a Seitung harbormaster." At least, in polite company.

name: Tsumei Village
description: This pastoral agricultural community has remained virtually unchanged for almost a thousand years, and its temples and farmhouses are among the oldest examples of ancient Canthan architecture in the empire. Thanks to the preservation efforts of Master Togo, wealthy tourists from Kaineng City have so far been prevented from spoiling Tsumei Village's idyllic splendor and historic buildings.

description: This small village at the northeastern tip of Istan has a dual purpose. Located near Churrhir Fields, the training grounds for Sunspear recruits, Chahbek's docks make an excellent meeting place for new Sunspears. Also, the bluffs around the village provide a good vantage point to watch for corsair raids headed for the islands. As a result, Chahbek is often the first community targeted by such attacks.

name: Remains of Sahlahja
description: This ruined and crumbling city was once the home of King Sahlahjar, the last of his line. Sahlahjar's father had resisted Palawa Joko for years, but with Lord Joko's armies advancing, Sahlahjar gave into his fears and cut a deal with the undead lord. Shortly after, Sahlahjar's citadel was overrun by Joko's undead army. The unlucky king was gutted and his remains animated as Joko's court jester. Sahlahjar remains bitter about this.

name: Gadd's Encampment
description: This ramshackle and temporary collection of buildings is the base of the Asuran Elementalist, Gadd, who has been investigating the nature of a nearby Bloodstone. Because Gadd cares little for comfort, rest, or visitors, the settlement is quite spartan and harsh, with little in the way of amenities, or even permanent structures.

name: Umbral Grotto
description: Tucked beneath the dark granite of the mountain fastness, the Umbral Grotto is a lurking place for those who wish to keep their activities shrouded in shadow. The caverns beneath are overrun with Stone Summit Dwarves from the southern Shiverpeaks, making the grotto a dangerous place to wander.

name: Rata Sum
description: The hub of Asuran activity on the surface world, Rata Sum was quickly and magically erected when the race arrived from their native underground homes. Geomystic generators dot the area, providing free power to the town. Some find the atmosphere within the town uncomfortable, saying you can literally feel the Energy being sucked from the air, but the Asura vow this enchanted technology is "perfectly safe."

name: Tarnished Haven
description: Founded by exiles from Kryta, this settlement is a common destination for political refugees. Those who find themselves "on the outs" with the current ruling faction in Lion's Arch come here to hide from the political upheaval rampant within the Krytan state. As a result, the haven's inhabitants are a combination of expatriates, agents, spies, and refugees.

name: Eye of the North
description: The origin of the Eye of the North is so ancient it has been lost to even the wisest skaald, the cultural storytellers of the Norn. Currently, the massive structure has become a base of operations for a group of Ascalonian expatriates known as the Ebon Vanguard, who plan and execute raids against the Charr from within the safety of its walls.

name: Sifhalla
description: Sif Shadowhunter refused to battle for an encampment held by other Norn, instead building her own hearthstead and defending it so fiercely that some call it "Bear Mother's Cave" in tribute to her strength and glory. Others of similar attitude have put up hides here, describing notorious foes they plan to hunt, or daring others to track them down.

name: Gunnar's Hold
description: The armorer, Gunnar Poundfist, claims current ownership over this massive hearthstead, the longest-occupied of all Norn settlements. The great hold has changed names numerous times over the years, controlled and claimed by many powerful Norn. Gunnar is a notable smith, a profession that earns great respect within the Norn community; enough so that Poundfist's claim on Gunnar's Hold has stood for quite some time, as most other Norn are wary of losing his good will.

name: Olafstead
description: Home of Olaf Olafson, the seventh Olaf in his family line, this squat, hilltop fort overlooks Varajar Fells. The grass-covered keep is a haven for Norn hunters to rest between battles and tell tales by the fireside. Olaf is also the reigning champion of Great Norn Alemoot, and his notoriety draws younger Norn to his fireside to hear stories of his mighty battles.

description: This dark shrine radiates heat and magic, a testament to ancient days of Charr domination and worship to their former gods, the Titans. Now, in the absence of these deities, the shrine has become a haven for the Charr Shaman caste. An entrance at the shrine leads to a sprawling complex beneath known as the Cathedral of Flames.

name: Longeye's Ledge
description: This steep, sloping hillside overlooking green Charr lands is the home of Olfun Longeye. The ledge overlooks a passage for both Charr and human raiding parties alike, and many travelers use this hearthstead as a stopping point during long journeys. Olfun has made it clear to all: any fighting on his land will not be tolerated, and shall be punished severely.

The Asura channel that raw power to fuel all the gates in the network and link them together via this great crossroads of transport. Most of the major gates across Tyria lead to this location.

It is muttered among the Norn that old Feodor is alive somewhere deep beneath his home, lost in Asura lands, protesting the invasion with a hammer and shield.

description: As the ancient Canthan name implies, Shing Jea is the jewel of Cantha. Headed by the legendary Ritualist, Master Togo, the monastery provides training to students of all heroic professions, including the Ritualist and Assassin professions native to Cantha. Graduates of the Shing Jea Monastery are recognized worldwide as masters of their chosen arts.

name: Kaineng Center
description: This area of Cantha's sprawling northern metropolis is also sometimes called "Old Kaineng" and is usually among the first stops for visitors to the Empire of the Dragon. Before the Jade Wind, the place now called Kaineng Center actually comprised most of Kaineng City, but the ensuing population explosion as citizens fled the affected regions led to an equal expansion of metropolitan boundaries. The central district's new, official moniker was approved by imperial decree in 1408 CC.

name: Kamadan, Jewel of Istan
description: Kamadan is the home port for the mighty Istani navy, and the main point of landfall for ships from nearby Kourna, as well as those traveling from Cantha, Tyria, and the Battle Isles. Its deep harbor is sheltered from seasonal storms by a ridge of hills to the south. Built around relics and statues from the days of the Primeval Kings, Kamadan has earned the title, Jewel of Istan.

Shing Jea Arena, located on the tiny island of Tinnairukan south of the larger landmass...close enough to train, but separated from Shing Jea Island itself.
